title: Word Search II
prompt:
Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` (a list of lists, one character per cell) and a list of strings `words`, return all words from `words` that can be formed by a path through adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically neighboring, not diagonal). The same cell may not be used more than once within a single word's path, but each word search starts fresh (a cell can be reused across different found words).

Return the found words sorted alphabetically, for deterministic comparison.

examples.explanation: "oath" traces o->a->t->h through adjacent cells. "eat" traces e->a->t. "pea" and "rain" cannot be traced. Sorted alphabetically: ["eat","oath"].
"abcb" would require reusing the cell containing 'b', which isn't allowed within a single word's path.
A single-cell board trivially matches a single-letter word with no adjacency steps needed.

constraints: board[i][j] is a lowercase English letter
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Searching each word independently with a fresh DFS from every cell works, but for many words it's much faster to combine them all into a single trie first, so shared prefixes are only explored once.
Do one DFS pass over the board; at each cell, walk down the trie as far as the board's letters allow, rather than restarting a trie lookup per word.

Mark a trie node's matched word (store the full word string at its end-of-word node) so that when your DFS reaches an end-of-word node, you can record it directly. Mark visited cells during the DFS path and unmark them on backtrack, and consider pruning a trie leaf after it's found to avoid duplicate work.

solution.approach: Build a trie from all words, storing the complete word string at each end-of-word node for easy retrieval. Then do a single DFS from every board cell: at each step, check if the current board character exists as a child in the current trie node; if so, descend the trie alongside moving to the neighbor cell. Whenever a trie node marked as a word-end is reached, add that word to the results (and clear the marker to avoid duplicate additions). Mark cells visited during the current path with a sentinel to prevent reuse, and restore them when backtracking. Finally, sort the found words alphabetically for deterministic output.
solution.timeComplexity: O(m * n * 4 * 3^(L-1)) worst case, where L is the max word length, bounded by trie sharing across words
solution.spaceComplexity: O(total characters across words) for the trie
